sections.description: David dies, Solomon secures the throne

sections.title: The Kingdom Divided
sections.description: Solomon's downfall and the division of the kingdom

sections.title: The Two Kingdoms
sections.description: Kings in the north and south

sections.description: The ministry of the prophet Elijah

events.title: Solomon Becomes King
events.description: The aging David appoints his son Solomon as king under pressure from Bathsheba and the prophet Nathan. Adonijah had attempted to seize power, but Solomon is anointed at the Gihon spring and placed on the throne while David is still alive.

events.title: David's Farewell and Death
events.description: David gives Solomon his final exhortations: to remain faithful to the Lord and follow His commands. He also gives instructions concerning Joab and Shimei. David dies after reigning for 40 years—seven years in Hebron and 33 years in Jerusalem.

events.title: Solomon Secures the Throne
events.description: Solomon consolidates his power by dealing with his opponents. Adonijah is executed after requesting Abishag, Abiathar is banished from the priesthood, and Joab and Shimei are put to death. Solomon's kingdom is now firmly established.

events.title: Solomon's Wisdom
events.description: God appears to Solomon in a dream at Gibeon and invites him to ask for whatever he desires. Solomon asks for a listening heart to govern the people justly. God grants him unmatched wisdom, along with wealth and honor. Solomon's wisdom is demonstrated in the judgment between the two mothers.

events.title: Solomon's Administration and Wisdom
events.description: Solomon organizes the kingdom with twelve district governors who provide supplies. His wisdom surpasses all the wise men of the East and the wisdom of Egypt. He composes 3,000 proverbs and 1,005 songs, and people from all nations come to hear his wisdom.

events.title: Temple Construction Begins
events.description: In the fourth year of Solomon's reign, construction of the Lord's temple begins. Solomon makes an agreement with King Hiram of Tyre for the delivery of cedar and cypress trees. 30,000 men are sent to Lebanon in shifts, and 150,000 work on stone and transport.

events.title: Solomon's Palace
events.description: Solomon builds his own palace complex, which takes thirteen years to complete. It includes the House of the Forest of Lebanon, the Hall of Pillars, the throne room, and his private residences. The craftsman Hiram from Tyre makes the bronze pillars and all the furnishings.

events.title: The Temple is Dedicated
events.description: Solomon gathers all Israel to bring the ark of the covenant into the temple. The glory of the Lord fills the house like a cloud, so that the priests cannot stand and serve. Solomon offers his great dedication prayer and asks God to hear every prayer directed toward this house.

events.title: God Appears to Solomon Again
events.description: The Lord appears to Solomon a second time and promises to let His name dwell in the temple forever. But He warns: If Solomon or his descendants turn away and worship other gods, Israel will be torn from the land and the temple rejected.

events.title: The Queen of Sheba
events.description: The queen of Sheba comes to test Solomon's wisdom with difficult questions. She is overwhelmed by his wisdom, wealth, and splendor, and exclaims that not even half had been told her. She gives him gold, spices, and precious stones.

events.title: Solomon's Wealth and Splendor
events.description: Solomon received 666 talents of gold annually. He made 200 large shields of gold and a great ivory throne overlaid with gold. All his drinking vessels were of gold. His merchant fleet sailed to Tarshish and brought back gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.

events.title: Solomon's Fall and Idolatry
events.description: Solomon loved many foreign women—700 wives and 300 concubines. They turned his heart to other gods: Ashtoreth, Chemosh, and Milcom. The Lord became angry and warned that the kingdom would be torn from his son, but for David's sake one tribe would remain.

events.title: Solomon's Adversaries Arise
events.description: God raised up adversaries against Solomon: Hadad the Edomite and Rezon from Damascus. The prophet Ahijah from Shilo tore his new cloak into twelve pieces and gave ten to Jeroboam as a sign that he would become king over ten tribes.

events.title: The Kingdom Divides: Rehoboam and Jeroboam
events.description: After Solomon's death, the people came to Rehoboam at Shechem and asked for lighter burdens. Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders and threatened even harsher treatment. Ten tribes rebelled and chose Jeroboam as king over Israel. Only Judah and Benjamin remained with Rehoboam.

events.title: Jeroboam's Golden Calves
events.description: Jeroboam feared that if the people continued to go up to the temple in Jerusalem, they would return to Rehoboam. He made two golden calves and set them up in Bethel and Dan, saying: "See, these are your gods, Israel, who brought you up out of Egypt." He also appointed priests who were not from the tribe of Levi.

events.title: The Man of God from Judah
events.description: A man of God from Judah prophesied against the altar in Bethel and warned that a king named Josiah would one day burn human bones on it. The altar split as a sign. But the man of God was deceived by an old prophet into breaking God's command, and he was killed by a lion on his way home.

events.title: Asa of Judah
events.description: Asa reigns for 41 years and does what is right in the Lord's eyes. He removes idols, deposes his grandmother Maaka because she made an abominable idol, and restores the holy articles to the temple. But the high places are not removed.

events.title: Omri Founders Samaria
events.description: After a civil war in Israel, Omri becomes sole king. He buys the hill of Samaria and builds a new capital there. Omri does what is evil in the Lord's eyes, worse than all who came before him. He is regarded as the founder of a new dynasty in the northern kingdom.

events.title: Ahab Becomes King
events.description: Ahab, son of Omri, becomes king over Israel and is considered the worst of all kings. He marries Jezebel, daughter of the king of Sidon, and begins to worship Baal. He builds a temple for Baal in Samaria and does more to provoke the Lord than any king before him.

events.title: Elijah and the Drought
events.description: The prophet Elijah from Tishbe proclaims that no rain or dew will fall until he says so. God sends him first to the brook Cherith, where ravens bring him food, then to a widow in Zarephath. The widow's flour and oil do not run out, and Elijah raises her dead son.

events.title: Elijah on Mount Carmel
events.description: After three years of drought, Elijah challenges the 450 prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel. They call out to Baal all day without an answer. Elijah builds an altar, pours water over it, and prays to the Lord. Fire falls from heaven and consumes the sacrifice. The people cry out: "The Lord, he is God!" The prophets of Baal are killed, and rain comes.

events.title: Elijah Flees to Horeb
events.description: Jezebel threatens Elijah with death. In despair, he flees to the wilderness and asks to die. An angel gives him food and water, and he travels for 40 days to God's mountain, Horeb. There God speaks to him—not in the wind, earthquake, or fire, but in a still, gentle whisper. God gives him new tasks and reveals that 7,000 in Israel have not bowed their knee to Baal.

events.title: Ahab's War Against Aram
events.description: Ben-Hadad of Aram besieges Samaria with 32 kings. A prophet promises Ahab victory, and Israel defeats the Arameans twice. But Ahab spares Ben-Hadad's life against God's will, and a prophet declares that Ahab himself shall die in his place.

events.title: Naboth's Vineyard
events.description: Ahab wants Naboth's vineyard, but Naboth refuses to sell his ancestral inheritance. Jezebel arranges false witnesses who accuse Naboth of blasphemy, and he is stoned to death. Elijah meets Ahab in the vineyard and proclaims God's judgment: Dogs shall lick up Ahab's blood in that same place, and Jezebel's dynasty shall be wiped out.

events.title: Ahab's Death
events.description: Ahab and the king of Judah, Jehoshaphat, go to war against Aram to retake Ramoth in Gilead. The prophet Micaiah warns against the war and sees Israel scattered like sheep without a shepherd. Ahab disguises himself, but a random arrow strikes him between the armor plates. He dies at sunset, and dogs lick up his blood as Elijah had prophesied.
